canonical_statement: For a nonnegative measurable function on Euclidean space whose superlevel sets have finite measure, its Schwarz symmetric decreasing rearrangement is radial, nonincreasing in the radius, and equimeasurable with the original function.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: n : Nat with 0 < n; f : (Fin n -> Real) -> ENNReal (or an equivalent measurable-function encoding). Exact codomain and almost-everywhere quotient remain open.
quantifiers: nonnegative measurable f on Euclidean n-space
every positive superlevel set of f has finite Lebesgue measure
hypotheses: nonnegativity, represented either by the codomain or an explicit hypothesis
finite measure of {x | t < f x} for each t > 0
conclusion: Existence of a radial nonincreasing rearrangement f* with measure {x | t < f* x} = measure {x | t < f x} for every t > 0.

alternate_encodings.target: Define f* from the distribution function and generalized inverse
State equality of distribution functions modulo almost-everywhere equality

excluded_claims: rearrangements of signed or complex functions without first passing to absolute value
existence for functions whose positive superlevel sets have infinite measure
excluded_degenerate_cases: Dimension zero, infinite-measure positive superlevel sets, and ambiguity on measure-zero boundaries require explicit treatment before the statement is frozen.
